osWhy: When AI assistants recommend a business they read more than its own website: map services (Google Maps, Bing, Apple Maps), review and booking sites, and social profiles. When the name, address, phone number and opening hours are the same everywhere, it is easier for an assistant to recognise them as one business. This compares the store information registered in Nurevo with each listing.
osNoGuarantee: Consistent listings do not guarantee that an assistant will show or rank the business.

guidance.static.title: Not on WordPress: put these three on your site
guidance.static.lead: Most AI crawlers do not run JavaScript. Put the three items below directly into your site's HTML and server so they can be read without JavaScript.
guidance.static.stale: This is a static copy. When you change your store info, copy the JSON-LD and llms.txt again and replace them (they do not update by themselves).
guidance.static.jsonldHow: Paste it directly inside the <head> of your site's HTML and publish (on Wix, STUDIO and similar builders, use the custom code <head> field). Do not add it through Google Tag Manager: GTM inserts it with JavaScript, so most AI crawlers never see it.
guidance.static.llmsHow: Save it as a text file named llms.txt and upload it to your site root (https://your-domain/llms.txt).
guidance.static.robotsHow: Add them to the end of your site's robots.txt. They allow only the AI search crawlers and leave training crawlers (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, etc.) as they are. If robots.txt already has a group for the same User-agent, merge them.
guidance.static.off: JSON-LD delivery is turned off. Turn on "Serve JSON-LD" in the site settings.
guidance.static.failed: Could not load the paste-in data. Please reload the page.
guidance.static.tagHow: This tag only works when JavaScript runs in a browser. It measures AI-referred visits and helps browsers and AI agents that run JavaScript (WebMCP). Crawlers that do not run JavaScript never see what it adds, so it does not replace the three items above. The same applies when it is added through a GTM Custom HTML tag.

guide.content.title: Getting started
guide.content.intro: Five steps from adding a site to information AI can read.
guide.content.steps.0.2: Press "Add a site" and choose WordPress, Other website or No website yet.
guide.content.steps.1.1: Set it up for its type
guide.content.steps.1.2: WordPress: the plugin and a pairing code. Other websites: paste the JSON-LD, llms.txt and robots.txt lines. No website: list the hosted page URL.
guide.content.steps.2.2: Enter the name, address, phone, hours and so on on the site page and save.
guide.content.steps.3.2: "Run a diagnosis" shows the AEO score and how to fix each item.
guide.content.steps.4.2: Standard keeps up with the latest criteria automatically.
guide.content.articles.0.2:
"Add a site" starts by asking which site it is.
WordPress → install the plugin and connect it with a pairing code.
Other website (Wix, STUDIO, Squarespace, hand-written HTML…) → put the prepared JSON-LD, llms.txt and robots.txt lines on the site.
No website yet → Nurevo creates a hosted page (/s/) to list on Google Business Profile and similar.
guide.content.articles.1.2:
1. WordPress admin → Plugins → Add New, search for "Nurevo AEO" → Install → Activate.
2. On the site page in this dashboard, press "Issue a pairing code".
3. Paste the code into Nurevo AEO → Settings in WordPress admin and save.
4. On the same screen, make sure "Output AI-facing information for this site" is ON.
5. View the source of a public page and look for LocalBusiness in application/ld+json (clear the cache if you use a caching plugin).
guide.content.articles.2.2: Paste the generated JSON-LD directly into <head> (not via Google Tag Manager), upload llms.txt to the site root and add the robots.txt lines. Copy them again after changing store info. The optional tag.js only works where JavaScript runs (measurement, AI agents); crawlers that do not run JavaScript never see it.
guide.content.articles.3.2: Copy /s/slug to the Google Business Profile website field and Instagram profile.
guide.content.articles.4.2: Fill in the name, address, phone, hours, business type and so on in the form on the site page and save. On WordPress the plugin also syncs it. Only the real information you enter is given to AI.
guide.content.articles.5.2: "Run a diagnosis" on the site page shows the AEO score and the checks, each with how to fix it (on every plan). The prioritised fix list is part of Pro. "Scan (free)" only checks that the tag and schema are in the HTML.
guide.content.articles.6.2: Use the invitation URL to choose Store, Referrer, or Agency. Approval follows registration.
guide.payment.2: Under "Current plan" on the site page, press "Open payment page" for your own site, or "Copy link" and send it to a client. Stripe stores card details securely; Nurevo does not. To change plan, cancel or update the payment method, use "Change or manage plan" on the site page (the Stripe portal). The WordPress plugin picks up the plan on its next sync.
